transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um, thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. I guess I'm just here because I've been having a bit of a hard time lately with... well, just sitting. 

I mean, it's probably not a huge deal, but I'm in school right now to be a radiologic tech, and whenever I'm supposed to just sit quietly, like in a lecture or in the radiology suite, I get this really intense feeling like I'm... I don't know, like I'm crawling out of my skin? I've really been trying to just tough it out for months now, because I want to be professional and do a good job, you know? But no matter how hard I try, I always end up constantly shifting around, or pacing, or just finding some random excuse to get up and move. 

Is... is that something you can help with? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Does this feeling of crawling out of your skin only happen when you're sitting quietly in places like lectures or the radiology suite?

Um, well, I guess it's mostly when I'm supposed to be still? Like, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. It's just... yeah, lectures and the suite are the hardest because everyone else is so focused and quiet. But, um, I guess I feel it other times, too. Like if I'm at dinner with my family, or watching a movie, or just hanging out... I still kind of get that restless feeling. 

But I try really hard to hide it! Like, I don't want to be annoying to anyone. I usually just tap my foot or play with a pen so I'm not, you know, disrupting things. I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be difficult or anything, I just... I really struggle to just sit and relax. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you find that when you're feeling restless, you're also having thoughts that you can't stop thinking about or worries that are on your mind?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking, but it's not like I'm sitting there worrying about things or having, like, racing thoughts or anything. I don't want you to think I'm, you know, overly anxious or stressed out. 

It's really just a physical feeling in my body. Like my muscles just want to go. My mind is usually pretty clear, or at least, I'm just trying to focus on whatever I'm supposed to be doing, like paying attention to the instructor. I just... my body just won't cooperate. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right. I just don't really get those kinds of unstoppable thoughts or worries with it.
Do you feel upset or frustrated when you're experiencing this restless feeling?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I don't get, like, angry or anything. I hope I'm not coming across as someone who gets easily upset. It's more just... I guess I feel a little bad that I can't just be still like everyone else? 

Like, I know it's not a huge deal, and I really try not to let it bother me. It's just a little frustrating when I'm trying so hard to be professional and do the right thing, and my body just won't listen. But I don't want to make it sound like I'm having a meltdown over it or anything! It's just a mild annoyance, really. I hope that's an okay answer? I'm just trying to be honest without making it sound worse than it is.
Does this restless feeling happen at any specific time of day

Um, well, I don't think so? Like, I haven't really noticed it being worse in the morning or at night or anything like that. I hope that's okay to say? I don't want to sound like I'm not paying attention to my own body. 

It just sort of happens whenever I have to sit still for too long, no matter what time it is. Like, if I have an early morning class, I feel it then, but if I'm hanging out with my family in the evening, I feel it then, too. I try to just push through it, you know? I really hope I'm giving you the right information. Is there a certain time it's *supposed* to happen? I can try to pay closer attention if that would help you!
Are there any specific activities or situations where you don't feel this restless feeling, even if you have to sit still?

Um, honestly... I can't really think of any? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just, you know, completely out of control or not trying hard enough. I really do try my best to sit still whenever I'm supposed to! 

It's just that... yeah, if I have to sit down for a while, whether I'm in a lecture or even just trying to watch a movie or something, that feeling is pretty much always there. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm just bouncing off the walls constantly—I definitely try to keep it together and be polite. But the actual feeling inside my body? It doesn't really go away just because I'm doing something fun or relaxing. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture without making it sound worse than it is.
Do you feel sad when this restless feeling is happening?

Um, no, not really sad. I mean, I don't get depressed about it or anything like that. I hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm, like, unhappy with my life or anything? 

I feel pretty good most of the time! It's just... maybe a little annoying, like I said before. But definitely not sad. I don't want you to worry that I'm dealing with anything super heavy like depression on top of this. I'm just a normal guy who has a little trouble sitting still, you know? I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and not making things sound more dramatic than they actually are.
Do you feel anxious when this restless feeling is happening?

Um, anxious? No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious. Like, my heart isn't racing from worry or anything like that. I hope that's okay to say? I just really don't want you to think I'm, like, a super nervous wreck or anything. 

I mean, I guess it can be a tiny bit frustrating sometimes, just because I know I'm supposed to be sitting quietly, but it's definitely not anxiety. I'm usually pretty chill about things! I just have that... that buzzing feeling in my legs or whatever. But I'm not stressing out about life or panicking. I hope I'm explaining that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need without making it sound like I have all these other issues going on. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like this restless feeling is related to anything going on inside you, like emotions or thoughts, even if it's not anxiety or sadness?

Um, emotions or thoughts? No, I don't think so. I really hope I'm not missing something obvious here, but... yeah, it doesn't feel like it's connected to what I'm thinking about. 

Like, I could be having a totally great day, just thinking about regular stuff—school, or work, or whatever—and I still just have that... that need to move. It's really just a physical thing, I promise. I don't have, like, racing thoughts or anything crazy going on up there. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to be super clear that my head is in a good place. I'm just, you know, a little fidgety. Does that help answer your question? I'm trying my best to give you the right details!
Has this restless feeling affected your relationships with friends or family?

Um, my relationships? No, not really. I mean, my friends and family are super great, and we get along fine. I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm hard to be around or anything? 

Like, maybe my mom gets a little annoyed sometimes if we're at a restaurant and I keep bouncing my leg or getting up to go to the bathroom, but it's just normal family stuff, you know? Nobody's mad at me or anything. I try really hard to be a good friend and a good son. I don't want you to think I'm, like, ruining dinners or driving people away. Everyone's really understanding. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure you know I have a good support system and I'm not, like, a burden on anyone.
Has this restless feeling affected your ability to complete your schoolwork or duties as a radiologic tech student?

Um... schoolwork? Well, I mean, I try really, really hard to do a good job. I really do. I want to be a great tech. But, um... I guess it has caused a little bit of a hiccup lately? I hope you don't think I'm a bad student or anything. 

It's just... some of my clinical evaluations haven't been super great recently. My supervisors, they... they said I was kind of disrupting the patient flow and making teamwork a little harder? Just because I'm always moving around or jumping from one thing to another. So, um, they actually put me on a formal remediation plan. 

I'm really embarrassed to even say that, honestly. I don't want you to think I'm failing on purpose or that I don't care. I just... I really need to get it under control because I'm kind of terrified it might cost me my spot in the program if I don't fix it. I'm trying to fix it, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like a total mess.
Do you think you feel this way because you get bored when sitting still?

Um, bored? No, I wouldn't say it's because I'm bored. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I don't care about what's going on around me, because I do! I'm actually really interested in my classes and the clinicals. 

It's not like I'm sitting there thinking, "Oh, this is so dull, I need to do something else." It's more just... my body just wants to go, even when my brain is totally engaged. I could be doing something I really love and still feel like I need to shift around or stand up. I try to stay focused, I really do. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm slacking off or not paying attention because I'm bored. I'm really trying my best to be present. Is that a helpful answer?
Are there any specific situations or environments where your restless feeling is more intense or less intense?

Um... specific situations? Gosh, I'm not really sure. I hope it's okay that I don't have a great answer for that. I really want to give you the right information, but... it just kind of feels like it's always there? Like, no matter where I am. 

I try so, so hard to keep it under wraps everywhere I go so I don't bother anyone. I guess maybe I don't think about it as much when I'm already walking around or doing something active, but the actual feeling inside doesn't really go away. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not very helpful. Is it bad that I haven't noticed a pattern? I can definitely try to pay more attention to it this week if that's what you need me to do! I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think your restless feeling is ever triggered by a specific emotional state?

Um, an emotional state? Like, being sad or mad or something? I... I don't think so. I really hope that's an okay answer. I don't want to sound like I'm not in touch with my feelings or anything. I try to be really self-aware! 

But honestly, it's just kind of... always humming in the background, you know? It doesn't really seem to matter if I'm having a great day or a stressful day. I mean, I guess if I'm super stressed about a clinical exam, I might fidget a tiny bit more? But the actual feeling of needing to move, that restless motor running inside me... it's just sort of my baseline, I guess. 

I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. Should I be looking for emotional triggers? Because I can totally start keeping a journal if you think that would help us figure this out. I just want to be as helpful as possible for you.
Are there any physical activities or exercises that make your restless feeling better or worse?

Um, physical activities? Gosh, I... I really haven't noticed if working out changes it. I hope that's alright to say! I mean, I try to stay somewhat active, you know, just to be healthy and everything. But as for making that feeling go away... I don't think so? 

Even if I go for a run or something, once I stop and sit down, that humming feeling is just right there waiting for me. It doesn't really seem to get better or worse based on exercise. I'm sorry, I know I keep giving you these "I don't know" kind of answers. I really don't want you to think I'm not trying to be observant! Is it normal that exercise doesn't really fix it? I can definitely try doing different types of workouts if you think that might help me give you a better answer next time!
Do you ever have periods during the day where you don't feel restless at all?

Um... periods where I don't feel restless at all? Gosh, I... I don't think so? I really hope it's okay that I'm saying that. I don't want to sound like I'm exaggerating or being difficult or anything! I try really hard to just push through it and be a good student in my radiology program. 

But honestly, it just feels like it's always there. Even when I'm trying to relax or go to sleep, my brain and my body just feel like they need to be doing something. I mean, I guess when I'm actually asleep I don't feel it, but other than that... no, not really. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just giving you the same answer over and over again! Am I doing this wrong? I really want to be helpful and give you the right information. If I need to try harder to find moments where I'm completely still, I absolutely will! I just want to make sure I'm doing what you need me to do.
Have you experienced any other symptoms besides the restless feeling, such as difficulty concentrating or remembering things?

Um, difficulty concentrating or remembering things? Oh, gosh... I mean, I really don't think so? I hope that's the right answer. I try so, so hard to be on top of everything, especially with my classes and clinicals. I don't want to sound like a bad student or like I'm slacking off! 

I mean, I get good grades and I always make sure I study. Sometimes I might have to read a page a couple of times, but that's just normal, right? Everyone gets a little distracted sometimes. But as for like, a real problem with memory or focus... no, I don't think I have that. I'm pretty sure my memory is fine. 

I'm really sorry if that's not helpful! Should I be having trouble with my memory? I can definitely try to pay more attention to how I study if you think I might be missing something. I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on!
Do you have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your schoolwork or other activities?

Um, careless mistakes? Gosh, I really hope not! I mean, especially with the radiology stuff, details are just so important, you know? I try to be so, so careful with everything I do. 

I really don't think I have a problem with missing details. I mean, I always try to double-check my work because I really want to do a good job and impress my instructors. Sometimes I might rush through an assignment just a tiny bit because I have all that pent-up energy, but I always try to go back and catch anything I missed. That's just a normal thing everybody does, right? 

I hope it's okay to say that I don't really struggle with that part. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything or make myself look better! I just really try my hardest to be thorough. Is it bad if I say no to that one? I can definitely ask my clinical supervisor if she's noticed me making mistakes, if you think I might just be missing it! I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Did you have trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were a kid?

Um, when I was a kid? Oh, gosh... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I always tried to be good, I promise. But, um... yeah, my parents actually still talk about my elementary school parent-teacher conferences. 

They always tell this story—and I hope it's okay to share this, I don't want to sound like a troublemaker—but the teachers used to say I was always popping out of my seat, or blurting things out, or just kind of rushing ahead to do things before they even finished giving the directions. 

So, I guess... yeah, that kind of stuff was happening way before middle school, definitely way before my radiology training. I really hope that's the kind of information you were looking for! I'm not trying to make excuses for how I acted back then, I just... I guess I've always had a lot of energy? Is it okay that I was like that as a kid? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right!
Did you ever receive a diagnosis of ADHD as a child?

Um, a diagnosis? Oh, gosh... no, I don't think I ever did. I really hope that's okay! I mean, my parents just kind of thought I was a really energetic boy, you know? They never actually took me to a doctor for it or anything. I always tried so, so hard to behave and keep my grades up, so I guess they didn't think there was anything officially wrong with me that needed a doctor. 

Is it bad that I wasn't diagnosed back then? I promise I'm not trying to waste your time or make a big deal out of nothing! I just... I really want to do things right and be the best tech I can be. I hope it's still alright that I'm here talking to you about this, even without having some kind of official record from when I was little. I just want to do whatever you think is best!
